feedback_rules.description: Distinguish between timing errors and expressive improvisation
Camera cannot assess cultural respect or community engagement

learning_units.description: Practice the cavalier's initial courtship dance display
Practice the dam's reactive dance movements
Learn call-and-response singing between chantwèl and lavwa
Follow the tibwa rhythm pattern on bamboo
Coordinate dance timing with bélé drum accents

prerequisites.description: Basic physical coordination and ability to follow rhythmic patterns

social_formats.description: Solo roles: cavalier and dam alternating dance turns
Group roles: chantwèl (lead singer), lavwa (chorus), tanbouyé (drummer), bwatè (tibwa player), audience participation
Formation: open space or circle with dancers in front of musicians and audience
Shared rhythm maintained by tibwa and drum, with vocal cues

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Graceful sweeping gestures and ceremonious bows
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Danced by a male-female couple in front of musicians and audience, often in a circle or open space
movement_profile.partnering: Courtship style with alternating solos and joint dancing
movement_profile.posture: Upright, elegant posture reflecting French ballroom influence combined with African groundedness

signature_moves.description: Male dancer shows off skill and courtship prowess
signature_moves.name: Cavalier display

signature_moves.description: Female dancer reacts to cavalier's movements
signature_moves.name: Dam response

signature_moves.description: Both dancers perform vigorous movements together
signature_moves.name: Joint wild dance

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Rhythmic and flowing, matching drum and tibwa patterns
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid disrespecting the call-and-response structure Avoid inappropriate imitation of sacred or ritual dances

music_profile.meter: not explicitly described, implied complex Caribbean rhythms
music_profile.musical_form: Entry of singer and chorus, followed by tibwa rhythm, then bélé drum, then dancers
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Tibwa plays a basic repeating pattern on bamboo; bélé drum marks accents and improvises
music_profile.vocal_style: Call-and-response between lead singer (chantwèl) and chorus (lavwa), with audience participation

basic_steps: Cavalier initiates with a display of dance skill
Dam responds with a reactive movement
Alternating turns between cavalier and dam
Joint vigorous dance in the climax
teaching.formation: Male-female couple dancing in front of musicians and audience, typically in an open or circular space
teaching.level_notes: Beginners start by learning the basic courtship steps and timing with the drum and tibwa; advanced dancers master improvisation and interaction with musicians
teaching.rhythm: Call-and-response singing with steady tibwa rhythm and accented bélé drum improvisations
